title: A Cup
simplified_paragraphs: 一个富人问禅师："我一生忙于赚钱，请问我应该赚多少才停止？”
禅师在桌子上放了一个杯子，然后用水壶给杯子倒水。水都溢满整张桌子了，禅师还是继续倒，直到把水壶里的水都倒完为止。
富人回答："我不明白这是什么意思？”
禅师说："整壶水是你一生所赚的钱，杯子的容量是你一生所需要花的钱，赚超过自己所需要的财富，只会溢出来，但不能留住。”
traditional_paragraphs: 一個富人問禪師："我一生忙於賺錢，請問我應該賺多少才停止？”
禪師在桌子上放了一個杯子，然後用水壺給杯子倒水。水都溢滿整張桌子了，禪師還是繼續倒，直到把水壺裡的水都倒完為止。
富人回答："我不明白這是什麼意思？”
禪師說："整壺水是你一生所賺的錢，杯子的容量是你一生所需要花的錢，賺超過自己所需要的財富，只會溢出來，但不能留住。”
pinyin_paragraphs: yī gè fù rén wèn chán shī：" wǒ yī shēng máng yú zhuàn qián， qǐng wèn wǒ yīng gāi zhuàn duō shao cái tíng zhǐ？”

chán shī zài zhuō zi shàng fàng le yī gè bēi zi， rán hòu yòng shuǐ hú gěi bēi zi dào shuǐ。 shuǐ dōu yì mǎn zhěng zhāng zhuō zi le， chán shī hái shi jì xù dào， zhí dào bǎ shuǐ hú lǐ de shuǐ dōu dào wán wéi zhǐ。
chán shī wèn：" nǐ dǒng le ma？”
fù rén huí dá：" wǒ bù míng bai zhè shì shén me yì si？”

chán shī shuō：" zhěng hú shuǐ shì nǐ yī shēng suǒ zhuàn de qián， bēi zi de róng liàng shì nǐ yī shēng suǒ xū yào huā de qián， zhuàn chāo guò zì jǐ suǒ xū yào de cái fù， zhǐ huì yì chu lai， dàn bù néng liú zhù。”
english_paragraphs: A wealthy man asked a Zen master, “I’ve spent my whole life making money. How much should I earn before I stop?”
The Zen master placed a cup on the table and began pouring water into it from a kettle. Even after the water overflowed and covered the entire table, he kept pouring until the kettle was empty.
The Zen master asked, “Do you understand now?”
The wealthy man replied, “I don’t understand what this means.”

The Zen master said, “The kettleful of water is all the money you earn in your lifetime, and the cup holds as much as you’ll need to spend. Anything you earn beyond what you need will simply overflow—you won’t be able to keep it.”
english_full:
A wealthy man asked a Zen master, “I’ve spent my whole life making money. How much should I earn before I stop?”

The Zen master placed a cup on the table and began pouring water into it from a kettle. Even after the water overflowed and covered the entire table, he kept pouring until the kettle was empty.

The Zen master asked, “Do you understand now?”

The wealthy man replied, “I don’t understand what this means.”

The Zen master said, “The kettleful of water is all the money you earn in your lifetime, and the cup holds as much as you’ll need to spend. Anything you earn beyond what you need will simply overflow—you won’t be able to keep it.”
